name: OkHttp
summary: OkHttp is an HTTP client for Java, Kotlin and Android. Your app builds a Request, hands it to an OkHttpClient, and gets a Response back. In between, every request passes through a chain of interceptors that handles retries, headers, caching and connections, so your code never deals with sockets, TLS or HTTP/2 directly.

groups.label: Public API
groups.description: The classes your code uses directly.

groups.label: Request pipeline
groups.description: Interceptors, run in this order for every request. Each can change the request, answer it, or pass it on.

groups.label: Connections
groups.description: Finding a server and keeping sockets open for reuse.

groups.label: Protocols and platform
groups.description: Bytes on the wire, TLS, and background work.

groups.label: Optional modules
groups.description: Separate artifacts you add when you need them.

nodes.label: Your code
nodes.description: Builds a Request, calls the client, reads the Response. Usually keeps one OkHttpClient for the whole app.

nodes.label: OkHttpClient
nodes.description: Holds all configuration: timeouts, interceptors, cache, cookie jar, DNS, connection pool. Creates a Call for each request. Share one instance so calls can reuse connections and threads.

nodes.label: Request and Response
nodes.description: Immutable HTTP messages: URL, method, headers and body. HttpUrl parses and builds URLs; Headers holds header fields.

nodes.label: Call
nodes.description: One request in flight. execute() runs it on your thread; enqueue() runs it in the background and calls you back. RealCall builds the interceptor chain and can be cancelled.

nodes.label: Dispatcher
nodes.description: Runs enqueued calls on a thread pool and limits how many run at once: 64 in total and 5 per host by default. Extra calls wait in a queue.

nodes.label: WebSocket
nodes.description: newWebSocket() upgrades an HTTP call to a WebSocket, then keeps the connection open to send and receive messages.

nodes.label: Your interceptors
nodes.description: Added with addInterceptor(). Run first and once per call, before retries and redirects. Typical uses: logging, auth headers, metrics.

nodes.label: Retry and redirects
nodes.description: Retries after recoverable connection failures, follows 3xx redirects, and asks the Authenticator for credentials when a server or proxy replies 401 or 407.

nodes.label: Bridge
nodes.description: Turns your request into a network request: adds Host, User-Agent, Content-Length, Accept-Encoding: gzip and cookies from the CookieJar. On the way back it saves cookies and unzips the body.

nodes.label: Cache
nodes.description: If a Cache is configured, answers from disk when HTTP caching rules allow, sends conditional requests when a cached copy is stale, and stores cacheable responses.

nodes.label: Connect
nodes.description: Gets a connection for this request, either a pooled one or a brand new one, and opens an Exchange: one request and response on that connection.

nodes.label: Network interceptors
nodes.description: Added with addNetworkInterceptor(). See the request exactly as sent, including redirects and retries, and the raw response before it is unzipped.

nodes.label: Call server
nodes.description: The last step. Writes the request headers and body to the connection and reads the response back.

nodes.label: Route planner
nodes.description: Decides how to reach the server: DNS lookup, which proxy, which IP address to try next. Remembers routes that failed recently so it tries others first.

nodes.label: Connection pool
nodes.description: Keeps idle connections open so later requests to the same server skip the TCP and TLS handshake. By default holds 5 idle connections for up to 5 minutes.

nodes.label: Connection
nodes.description: One socket to one server. Connecting means TCP connect, TLS handshake, and agreeing on HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2. Can be shared by many requests over time.

nodes.label: HTTP/1.1
nodes.description: Writes one request and reads one response at a time on a connection.

nodes.label: HTTP/2
nodes.description: Runs many requests at once as separate streams over a single connection.

nodes.label: Platform and TLS
nodes.description: Hides differences between Android, JVM versions and security providers: setting up TLS, ALPN protocol negotiation, hostname checks and certificate pinning.

nodes.label: Task runner
nodes.description: OkHttp's own background scheduler. Runs connection pool cleanup, HTTP/2 writers and timeouts.

nodes.label: Logging interceptor
nodes.description: Logs requests and responses at a chosen level of detail. Add it as an interceptor.

nodes.label: DNS over HTTPS
nodes.description: A Dns implementation that resolves hostnames over HTTPS instead of the system resolver.

nodes.label: Server-sent events
nodes.description: Reads a stream of server-sent events from a long-lived response.

nodes.label: Coroutines
nodes.description: Call.executeAsync(): a suspend function for Kotlin coroutines.

nodes.label: MockWebServer
nodes.description: A scriptable local HTTP server for testing code that uses OkHttp.

nodes.label: Web server
nodes.description: The server being called. Outside OkHttp: it only sees bytes arriving on a socket.
